chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad and Fadalah from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyabah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about fish that are caught, then placed in something, then returned to the water, and die in it. He said, 'Do not eat it, because it died in that which is its life.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating fish that are caught, kept out of water, and then die after being returned to the water?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the ruling for fish caught and kept in a medium (such as water or air) before dying, declaring them inedible because they perished in the very substance that sustains their life. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the specific mode of death and the purity of the environment in which the animal expires, distinguishing it from fish that die naturally in the sea. The narration underscores the principle that the medium of death affects the ritual status (*taharah*) of the seafood, a key topic in the chapter of hunting and slaughter.
